findings.text: A class body local to a function is still counted as a second owner. The walk outward answers as soon as it reaches a Module or a ClassDef, so it never notices the FunctionDef above. Concrete input: a module imas_ambix/agent/local_class_grammar.py holding a def build_grammar() whose body binds a class Holder whose body is `_SAMPLE_RE = None`. With that module in the package, test_every_guarded_symbol_has_one_owner fails and names the module as an extra definer of _SAMPLE_RE, measured in this review as 1 failed, 8 passed in 14.54s on an all_debug allocation (logs/r8-function-local-class-in-package.txt, this review's run directory). The binding is a class attribute of a class that exists only while one call runs, so no caller can resolve through it and the module holds no copy of the grammar. The unit test that pins the sparing half of the two-sided rule covers an ordinary local variable only, so this narrower over-fire is unasserted in both directions. The probe's classification line reports the same module for _SAMPLE_RE (logs/shape-probe.log).

A module-level assignment expression inside a comprehension binds in the containing scope, so a module whose only content is the single line `pairs = [(_LABEL_RE := index) for index in range(3)]` exports _LABEL_RE for real. Running that module under runpy leaves _LABEL_RE among its module-level names (logs/shape-probe.log, the runtime-truth lines), while the scan reports no declaration of _LABEL_RE in that module (same log, the classification line for _LABEL_RE lists only the if/else module). A second owner written that way is invisible to the guard, and the rule's docstring at lines 116-124 states the comprehension case as local without that exception, which the walrus form falsifies.

One assertion in the delivered file derives its expected value from the module under test. The line at 387 compares the bench snapshot against engine_metrics.read_metrics(_SPEC_DECODE_SCRAPE).spec_decode, so both sides are computed by code under test and a defect moving both sides together stays green. The literal pins on the following four lines, 9560.0, 4418.0, [1423.0, 1108.0] and the two bounds, are what actually hold the content. The identical line exists at the reviewed base revision 5d8ce3d9 at line 123, so it predates this node's change and is recorded rather than attributed to the diff.
